findings.place: app/scripts/public-set.js lines 170-186 (htmlFiles takes a link named *.html as a page), 217-224 and 266-269 (texts.js read and written through a link), 287 (writeFileSync of a page through a link); app/scripts/vercel-build.js line 165 (fs.cpSync without verbatimSymlinks)
findings.what: The public-set writer follows symbolic links, so a write can leave its folder. Measured under <scratch>: (W1b) an upload whose linked.html is a link to a page outside the upload — writePublicSet rewrote the outside page (its order region cut) and listed linked.html as changed; (W2) a source app/public whose shared/i18n/texts.js is a relative link — runBuild into another output folder copied it as an absolute link back to the source (fs.cpSync resolves relative links) and rewrote the source file, exit 0 «vercel-build: done»; the in-place refusal inside a git tree does not cover this path. Control W3 without links: nothing outside changed. check-public (step 3 of the build) does not refuse links, and the static server silently skips them. The precondition is a link committed into app/public (repository write access), and none exists today, so the risk is low; the protection the role asks for («neither through .. nor through a link») is missing.
findings.fix: In writePublicSet, before the first write, lstat every entry of the walk and refuse with an Error naming the file any symbolic link (a page, shared/i18n/texts.js, a folder, examples.html); in vercel-build.js refuse a link in the source before the copy (or copy with verbatimSymlinks: true and let the refusal of writePublicSet act); a test row for each (a page link, a texts.js link, a folder link, a relative link copied into another output) that is red today and green after the fix. Alternatively check-public refuses any link under the served folder, since it runs first in the build and in npm run check.

findings.place: app/server/routes/demo.js lines 39-61 (loadIntake's shape rule) and 134-151 (the questionnaire projection, outside a try); app/server/app.js line 146 (a non-HttpError goes to onError)
findings.what: loadIntake accepts an intake whose questions hold an options array, but the questionnaire reads o.id and o.label of every option and runs inLanguage outside a try. Measured with test copies: an option that is null and an intake with a field nested 20 000 deep pass loadIntake, and then GET /api/demo/questionnaire answers 500 server_error (through onError) while POST /api/demo/result answers 503 demo_unavailable (its engine call is inside a try); two more shapes (a solution without includes, a rule with an unknown solution) give questionnaire 200 and result 503. The app keeps answering, every other route is unchanged and the page shows its message, so Q10 is met; the two routes just name the same broken intake with two codes, and criterion 7's «one stable code» holds only for the shapes loadIntake refuses. The content step (picker check) refuses such files before a release.
findings.fix: Either widen loadIntake to the fields the routes read (every option an object with a string id and a {ru, kk, en} label, every title a text object) so that such an intake is refused at the start (503 on both routes), or put the questionnaire projection inside the same try that maps an exception to demo_unavailable; a DM-6 row with an option that is null.
